# Calibrate treatment-effect *predictions.* {.unlisted .unnumbered}

::: {.intro}
`causalCalibration` adjusts predictions from a treatment-effect model so that people with the same calibrated score have an average treatment effect close to that score. Use it with predictions from your existing model, then estimate how much calibration error remains.
:::

::: {.hero-actions}
[Install and get started](getting-started.html){.primary-link}
[Worked examples](getting-started.html#full-examples)
:::
:::

::: {.hero-example}
## Fit a calibration map {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Supply predictions, treatment and outcome data, and estimates of the outcome regressions and propensity score.

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Python {.unlisted .unnumbered}

```python
from causal_calibration import fit_calibrator

cal = fit_calibrator(
    predictions=tau_hat,
    treatment=a, outcome=y,
    mu0=mu0_hat, mu1=mu1_hat,
    propensity=e_hat,
    loss="dr", method="isotonic",
)
tau_calibrated = cal.predict(tau_new)
```

### R {.unlisted .unnumbered}

```r
library(causalCalibration)

cal <- fit_calibrator(
  predictions = tau_hat,
  treatment = a, outcome = y,
  mu0 = mu0_hat, mu1 = mu1_hat,
  propensity = e_hat,
  loss = "dr", method = "isotonic"
)
tau_calibrated <- predict(cal, tau_new)
```
:::

This example uses a separate calibration sample. For cross-fitted models, use [cross-calibration](cross-calibration.html).
:::
:::

## Choose how to calibrate

::: {.section-lead}
The package supports binary treatments and observed outcomes. You supply treatment-effect predictions and nuisance estimates; the package fits the calibration map and computes diagnostics.
:::

::: {.guide-grid}
::: {}
### Standard calibration

Use `fit_calibrator()` with predictions on a separate calibration sample. Apply the fitted map to new predictions.

[Fit a calibrator](standard-calibration.html)
:::

::: {}
### Cross-calibration

Use `fit_cross_calibrator()` with out-of-fold predictions and a matrix of predictions from each fitted model. No separate calibration sample is needed.

[Use cross-fitted predictions](cross-calibration.html)
:::

::: {}
### Diagnostics

Use `diagnose_calibration()` to estimate calibration error with a confidence interval and compare raw and calibrated predictions. Use `assess_overlap()` to check propensity scores.

[Check calibration](diagnostics.html)
:::
:::

## Choose the population and method

`loss="dr"` targets the original study population. `loss="r"` targets an overlap-weighted population, giving more weight to people whose treatment probabilities are closer to one half.

Choose isotonic calibration for a nondecreasing step function, a monotone spline for a smooth nondecreasing function, linear calibration for an intercept and nonnegative slope, or histogram calibration for binwise averages.

[Compare losses and methods](choosing-losses-and-methods.html) · [API reference](reference.html)
